subject: Planned: Preemptive I/O compatibility wave — regional schedule & customer impact
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.in>
To: infra-ops@acme-corp.com, j.sanders@paymentsco.com, partners-support@cloudco.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.in>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.in>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: Preemptive I/O compatibility wave — regional schedule & customer impact

Hello team,

I’m reaching out with a heads-up about a planned compatibility sweep we’ll run across several US regions the week of August 25. This is a proactive I/O compatibility wave (nonblocking) targeting a small set of NIC and driver variations that have produced intermittent client-side latency spikes in high-p99 tails.

High-level summary:
- What: staged, nonblocking updates and live patching to align kernel I/O paths and driver microcode across host pools; includes a KV-cache preservation routine to reduce cold-warm penalties.
- When: Aug 25–29, per-region windows (attached schedule grid). We'll run in US-West then US-East; see attachment for exact cut windows.
- Impact: anticipated customer-visible disruptions are low (<1% of requests at p99) when following KV-cache-preserve guidance. We will perform canaries before broad rollouts and have automatic rollback triggers.
- Opt-out: customers with strict latency SLAs can request exclusion from the wave for the scheduled week; reply with your region and customer tag.

Action items for customers:
1) Review the attached schedule (20250817-schedule-grid.csv) and confirm if you require opt-out by 48 hours before your region window.
2) If you have critical long-tail workloads, please reply with a short description (estimated p99 request size, consistent prefixes) so we can add targeted canaries.
3) Follow the included KV-cache playbook (kvcache-preserve-playbook.pdf) to minimize cold starts post-update.

Attachments: 20250817-schedule-grid.csv, kvcache-preserve-playbook.pdf

Marissa and Karthik — tagging you for runbook + rollback confirmations. I’ll coordinate final timing with the customer responses.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.in | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Acme Infra Ops <infra-ops@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.in>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned: Preemptive I/O compatibility wave — regional schedule & customer impact

Ben,

Thanks for the note. A couple quick questions from our side before we confirm:
1) Can you confirm the rollback SLA if the canary shows a regression? We need an expectation on time-to-restore for affected traffic.
2) For our high-throughput payment ingestion prefixes, should we expect any sustained increase in tail latency during the warm-up window even with KV-cache guidance applied?

We’ll aim to return an opt-out decision within 24 hours once we validate the specific time block.

— Alex (Acme Infra Ops)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.in>

Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned: Preemptive I/O compatibility wave — regional schedule & customer impact

Ben — quick internal sync before we reply to Acme.

Rollout and rollback notes:
- Canary approach: we’ll run a two-phase canary (5% then 25%) with 30–45 minute observation windows. If any regression in p50/p95/p99 or error rate is detected, the orchestration automatically stops further rollout and triggers host-level rollback to prior microcode snapshot.
- Time-to-restore: targeted RTO for rollback is sub-30 minutes for canary groups, sub-90 minutes for full pool rollbacks (including traffic resync). We’ll publish a short runbook snippet in the ops doc for Acme.
- Payment ingestion guidance: KV-cache playbook contains a small warmup script (warm_prefix_probe.sh) we recommend running immediately after your window to reduce elevated p99s. We still expect a short warm-up wiggle — typically 5–15 minutes for heavy-tail workloads — but with the script it should be negligible.

I’ve attached a trimmed runbook excerpt to the internal thread (not included in the customer attachment). Karthik: please confirm the orchestration stop criteria and that rollback snapshots are healthy for the affected west/us-east host pools.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Technical Program Manager, Customer Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.in

Alex / John / CloudCo team —

Thanks for the quick replies and the good questions. Short answers up-front: rollback SLA is as Marissa outlined (sub-30m canary, sub-90m full pool), and yes — the warmup script will materially reduce p99 exposure for payment ingestion prefixes.

Next steps:
- Acme: please confirm whether you’d like an opt-out for your US-West block by Aug 23 09:00 PT. If you’d like to stay in, run the warm_prefix_probe.sh immediately after your window and we’ll keep close monitoring on the canary.
- PaymentsCo: John, if you can share a single representative prefix and an expected qps range we’ll add a targeted canary to validate under load.
- CloudCo: we’ll post the final runbook links and the JIRA ticket (INF-7421) to your marketplace partner page; expect a doc push by end of day tomorrow.

Runbook + schedule: https://redwood.in/ops/IO-2025-wave
JIRA: INF-7421

If anything looks risky for your workloads, reply with the prefix + estimated 95/99 size and we’ll provision a hot rollback window. Otherwise we’ll assume opt-in and proceed with the canary schedule.

Contact: on-call SRE (Karthik) will be reachable at +1 (415) 555-0211 during the windows; I’ll be on the war-room channel as well.

Thanks,
Ben
